name: White Buffalo Calf Woman (Ptesáŋwiŋ)

domain_history.domain: sacred woman of supernatural origin who appeared during a famine, brought the Sacred (White Buffalo Calf) Pipe (Chanunpa) and the Seven Sacred Rites to the Lakota, then departed transforming into a white buffalo calf; culture-bringer, associated with the buffalo, fertility, and moral-law teaching

notes: Key text: Joseph Epes Brown, The Sacred Pipe: Black Elk's Account of the Seven Rites of the Oglala Sioux (University of Oklahoma Press, 1953). Internal dating per the Battiste Good winter count: c. 900 CE ("19 generations ago"), not externally corroborated.
